title: CLAUDE.md
text: Two core S4 classes flow pipeline: metaXpressStudy — output Module 1, input Modules 2–3. Extends SummarizedExperiment: - assay(study, "counts"): raw count matrix (genes × samples) - colData(study): sample metadata (must contain condition); study$condition works - rowData(study): optional gene annotation (e.g. gene_length TPM) - extra slots: accession, organism, qc_score, de_result - Build metaXpressStudy(); convert SE/DESeqDataSet mx_from_se() (se, "metaXpressStudy") - Never use study@metadata — SE free-form list, sample data. Internally use .counts(), .samples(), .set_counts() (R/utils.R) metaXpressResult — output Module 4, input Modules 5–8: - meta_table: gene-level results (meta-p, meta-FDR, meta-effect size, ²) - method, n_studies, heterogeneity, pathway_result

text: methods take return standard S4 objects — functions chain cleanly: mx_fetch_geo() → mx_filter_studies() → mx_reannotate() → mx_de_all() → mx_meta(). Per-study DE always run independently study meta-analysis (pooled). Missing genes across studies handled explicitly Module 5 (imputation coverage filtering), silently dropped. Meta-analysis methods supported: Fisher, Stouffer, inverse-normal (fused), fixed effects, random effects (DerSimonian-Laird), AWmeta adaptive weighting — selectable via method argument. Parallelization via BiocParallel throughout (parallel foreach). Indentation: 2 spaces (per .Rproj settings).

Choose question method seeing results. Random effects estimates average effect. maxP rOP ask whether gene changes studies. Picking whichever method gives genes inflates false findings. Make sure studies independent. Two GEO series lab brain bank may contain donors, count twice. Check donor case identifiers. Harmonise comparison. Every study must compare groups direction (case / control). Check fold-change concordance. Start raw counts. Run DE within study, adjusting known covariates sex batch. feed batch-corrected values count models (Nygaard et al. 2016). pooled effect confidence interval; I2I^2 τ2\tau^2; prediction interval; genes survive leave-one-analysis. cautious studies. fewer five studies, τ2\tau^2 imprecise. Tests publication bias (e.g. Egger’s test (Egger et al. 1997)) need ten studies (Sterne et al. 2011). Interpret pathways right level. Gene-set enrichment (Subramanian et al. 2005; Korotkevich et al. 2016; Liberzon et al. 2015) can run meta-signature, within study combined (Shen Tseng 2010). Remember tissue composition. bulk data, change cell-type proportions looks like change gene expression. Check cell-type marker scores (Becht et al. 2016).

title: metaXpress: End-to-End Bulk RNA-seq Meta-Analysis
text: Combining bulk RNA-seq studies usually patchwork: one package download GEO data, ad-hoc scripts QC gene ID mapping, separate DE run per study, another package meta-statistics, yet another pathways plots. hand-chance silently drop genes, mix identifiers, lose track study failed QC. metaXpress replaces patchwork one reproducible pipeline built two S4 objects pass cleanly step step. One workflow, end end. GEO ingestion → QC → harmonization → per-study DE → meta-analysis → pathways → figures → report, mx_* functions chain directly. Study quality explicit. data-level QC checklist fold-change concordance check (catches flipped contrasts) run pooling. Uniform quantification. default, counts come NCBI’s GEO RNA-seq pipeline, every study shares aligner, annotation counting. Statistically sound design. DE always run independently per study (DESeq2, edgeR limma-voom) combining — never pooled — avoiding batch-confounded inference. Choose right meta-method. Nine methods (random effects REML/PM/DL optional HKSJ, fixed effect, directional Fisher, Stouffer, weighted inverse-normal, minP, maxP, rOP, AWmeta) behind one method argument. Every gene gets tau², ², 95% CI prediction interval. Results validated metafor. Missing genes handled, hidden. gene pooled studies measured , n_studies reported. Genes never silently dropped intersect. Biology, just gene lists. fgsea GSEA/ORA meta-signature, per-study GSEA combined across studies, transcription factor activity, cell-composition meta-analysis, consensus co-expression modules drug-reversal ranking turn meta-signatures testable hypotheses. Publication-ready reproducible. Volcano, forest, heatmap, UpSet heterogeneity plots, plus HTML/PDF reports CSV/Excel export captured session info. Scales BiocParallel. Per-study steps parallelize box laptops clusters.

text: per-study results four cohorts ship package, analysis runs offline:
code: library(metaXpress)  # 1. Uniformly processed raw counts from GEO (NCBI pipeline) studies <- mx_fetch_geo(   c("GSE125583", "GSE104704", "GSE53697", "GSE173955"),   condition_col = c(GSE125583 = "diagnosis:ch1", GSE104704 = "study group:ch1",                     GSE53697 = "disease status:ch1", GSE173955 = "title"))  # 2. Per-study DE from raw counts, covariates and explicit contrasts studies <- mx_de_all(studies, method = "DESeq2",                      formula  = list(~ sex + condition, ~ condition,                                      ~ condition, ~ condition),                      contrast = list(c("Alzheimer's disease", "control"),                                      c("Aged, diseased", "Old"),                                      c("advanced Alzheimer's Disease", "control"),                                      c("Alzheimer's Disease", "non-Alzheimer's Disease"))) de_results <- lapply(studies, function(s) s@de_result)  # 3. Check orientation, then pool (random effects, REML) mx_study_concordance(de_results) res <- mx_meta(de_results, method = "random_effects", tau_method = "REML")  # 4. Robustness, pathways, figures, report loo <- mx_sensitivity(de_results, tau_method = "REML") res <- mx_pathway_meta(res, db = "Hallmarks")          # fgsea GSEA ps  <- mx_pathway_studies(de_results, db = "Hallmarks") # cross-study pathways mx_volcano(res); mx_forest("GFAP", de_results, res) mx_report(res, de_results, output_dir = "results") ad  <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ad_brain_de.rds", package = "metaXpress")) res <- mx_meta(ad$de_results)

text: metaXpress provides unified, reproducible pipeline integrating multiple bulk RNA-seq studies single meta-analysis. title: Compute per-gene heterogeneity statistics — mx_heterogeneity
code: set.seed(1) de <- lapply(1:3, function(s) {   lfc <- rnorm(50, s * 0.3, 0.2); se <- rep(0.2, 50)   p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(lfc / se))   data.frame(gene_id = paste0("G", 1:50), log2FC = lfc, lfcSE = se,              pvalue = p, padj = p.adjust(p, "BH")) }) het <- mx_heterogeneity(de) summary(het$I_sq) #>    Min. 1st Qu. Preferred comparing expression     levels across genes. quantile: Quantile normalization (Bolstad et al. 2003),     implemented limma. text: Initial Bioconductor submission. Module 1: Data ingestion GEO/SRA local files 10-point QC scoring. Module 2: Normalization (TMM, VST, CPM, TPM, quantile) batch correction (ComBat-seq, ComBat, limma, harmony). Module 3: Per-study differential expression via DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom. Module 4: Meta-analysis statistics — Fisher, Stouffer, inverse-normal, fixed effects, random effects (DerSimonian-Laird), AWmeta. Module 5: Missing gene handling imputation coverage filtering. Module 6: Pathway meta-analysis using KEGG, Reactome, GO, MSigDB Hallmarks. Module 7: Publication-ready visualization (volcano, forest, heatmap, UpSet plots). Module 8: Reproducible HTML/PDF report generation result export.
